newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on weak sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down across the board on Thursday on weak market sentiment, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 23,620 yuan ($2,848) per tonne, losing 30 yuan.
It opened at 23,700 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 23,700 and a low of 23,600.
May fell 50 to 23,030, June 80 to 23,310, July 80 to 23,500, August 40 to 23,590 and October 20 to 23,600.
Combined volume fell to 35,830 tonnes from 41,670.
Copper opened lttle changed from Wednesday's close and moved in a narrow range before speculative selling pushed it down late in the session.
Traders said many investors were not optimistic about the short-term market trend and wanted to liquidate positions.

"Despite overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, many Shanghai investors liquidated their long positions at high levels today," one trader said. "Many believed copper would not rise or fall sharply in the short term."
Physical prices are around 23,300 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area.
Analysts said they expected copper to move in a narrow range in the next few days with no market-moving news around the corner.
Aluminium ended mostly down. May rose 40 to 15,350, June fell 100 to 15,450, July lost 110 to 15,670 and August shed 120 to 15,900.
Combined volume fell to 1,650 tonnes from 1,970.
